title: 1. Set it up
description: One command, and a tour of what you get before writing a line.
sidebar:
  order: 1

import { Aside, Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components'

```bash
bun create theoven todo-api --db sqlite --auth basic
cd todo-api
bun install
```

<Steps>

1. **Set a signing secret.** The scaffold refuses to boot without one, on purpose — a framework
   that invents a secret has invented one every deployment shares.

   ```bash
   cp .env.example .env
   ```

   Open `.env` and put something in `AUTH_SECRET`:

   ```bash
   # macOS / Linux
   openssl rand -base64 32
   ```

2. **Create the database.**

   ```bash
   bun run db:generate    # writes a migration from your schema
   bun run db:migrate     # applies it
   ```

3. **Run it.**

   ```bash
   bun run dev
   ```

</Steps>

You now have a working API at `http://localhost:3000`, with browsable documentation at
[`/docs`](http://localhost:3000/docs).

```bash
curl -X POST localhost:3000/auth/signup \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"name":"Ada","email":"ada@example.com","password":"correct-horse"}'
```

That returns a user and an access token. You have not written any code.

## What you got

```
src/
  app.ts       builds the app — every brick registered here
  index.ts     starts the server
  env.ts       configuration, read and validated once at boot
  db.ts        the database brick
  client.ts    the connection, shared
  auth.ts      the auth provider
  mail.ts      the mail driver
  schema.ts    your tables
  routes/      the route table — the filesystem *is* the router
```

### `app.ts` is the whole configuration

```ts title="src/app.ts"
export const app = createApp({ logLevel: config.logLevel })
  .use(requestLogger())
  .use(securityHeaders())
  .use(database)
  .use(mail(driver))
  .use(auth(provider))
  .use(openapi({ info: { title: 'todo-api', version: '0.1.0' } }))

await loadRoutes(app, `${import.meta.dir}/routes`)
```

Six lines, and each one is a feature. `.use(auth(provider))` is what mounted those eight
`/auth/*` endpoints. `.use(database)` is what will put a typed client on every request.

Leave one out and the thing it provides becomes a **compile error** wherever you use it — not a
crash at 3am.

### `index.ts` is separate on purpose

```ts title="src/index.ts"
import app from './app'

await app.listen(config.port)
```

`app.ts` builds and exports; `index.ts` listens. That split is what lets `oven routes`,
`oven openapi` and your tests import the app without binding a port. Keep it.

### One connection, shared

```ts title="src/client.ts"
export const sqlite = new Database(config.databaseUrl)
export const client = drizzle(sqlite, { schema })
```

```ts title="src/db.ts"
export const database = db(drizzleSqlite({ client: sqlite, schema }))
```

`auth-basic` builds its user store at construction — before an app exists — so it needs a client
of its own. The database brick **adopts** that same connection rather than opening a second.

<Aside type="caution" title="This matters more than it looks">
  Two connections to a file merely waste a handle. Two connections to `:memory:` are two separate
  databases — and the symptom is `no such table` on a schema you can watch being created. You
  will want `:memory:` in [chapter 5](/docs/build/testing/), so it is worth knowing why this line
  reads the way it does.
</Aside>

### `env.ts` fails loudly

```ts title="src/env.ts"
function read() {
  return {
    port: env.port('PORT', 3000),
    databaseUrl: env.string('DATABASE_URL', './data.db'),
    authSecret: env.string('AUTH_SECRET'),
  }
}
```

`env.string('AUTH_SECRET')` has no default, so a missing one fails at **startup** with a message
naming the variable — rather than at 3am as `undefined` somewhere unrelated.

## Two things to try before moving on

**The API reference** at [`/docs`](http://localhost:3000/docs) is generated from your routes. It
already lists every auth endpoint. As you add schemas in the next chapter, it fills in.

**The mail inbox** at [`/_oven/mail`](http://localhost:3000/_oven/mail). Try a password reset:

```bash
curl -X POST localhost:3000/auth/forgot-password \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"email":"ada@example.com"}'
```

The reset link appears in that inbox and in your terminal, because mail defaults to the console
driver. The whole flow works before you have signed up for a mail provider.

## Clear the decks

The scaffold ships an example `users` resource to show the shape. You are building todos, so
delete it:

```bash
rm -rf src/routes/users src/routes/health.get.ts
```
